candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company invited applications for 2,00,000 equity shares from the public and received applications for only 1,80,000 shares. Assume the company has received the minimum subscription. For how many shares will the allotment be confirmed, following the treatment of under subscription in the NCERT text?

options.text: 2,00,000 shares, the number for which applications were invited
20,000 shares, the number of shares left unsubscribed
1,80,000 shares, the number of shares actually applied for
1,90,000 shares, the number used in the textbook example

candidate.explanation: Under subscription is a situation where the number of shares applied for is less than the number for which applications were invited. In the textbook example, where 2 lakh shares were offered and applications came for 1,90,000, allotment is confirmed to the shares applied for. Here applications are for 1,80,000 shares, so allotment is confirmed to 1,80,000 shares; 2,00,000 is the number invited, 20,000 is only the shortfall, and 1,90,000 belongs to the textbook example, not to this company.

learning_objective.objective: Explain the treatment of under subscription of shares at allotment.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company issues 10,000 equity shares of nominal value Rs. 50 each at Rs. 56 per share. The amount of premium is credited to a separate account called the Securities Premium Account. What amount is credited to the Securities Premium Account on the issue of these shares?
candidate.explanation: A share issued at an amount more than its nominal value is issued at a premium, so the premium is Rs. 56 - Rs. 50 = Rs. 6 per share. For 10,000 shares this is 10,000 x 6 = Rs. 60,000. Rs. 5,00,000 is 10,000 x 50, the nominal value; Rs. 5,60,000 is 10,000 x 56, the total issue price; Rs. 6,000 is 1,000 x 6, which applies the premium to only 1,000 shares.

learning_objective.objective: Compute the securities premium arising on issue of shares at a premium.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: Satish and Tilak are partners sharing profits equally. During the year, Satish withdrew Rs. 30,000 at the end of each quarter, that is Rs. 1,20,000 in all. Interest on drawings is charged at 8% per annum. Following the NCERT method for fixed amounts withdrawn quarterly, what is the interest on Satish's drawings?
candidate.explanation: When a fixed amount is withdrawn at the end of each quarter, interest is calculated on the total money withdrawn during the year for a period of 4.5 months. Interest = 1,20,000 x 8/100 x 4.5/12 = Rs. 3,600. Rs. 6,000 uses 7.5 months, which applies to withdrawals at the beginning of each quarter; Rs. 4,800 uses 6 months; Rs. 900 applies 4.5 months to only one withdrawal of Rs. 30,000.

learning_objective.objective: Calculate interest on partners' drawings when a fixed amount is withdrawn quarterly.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: X and Y are partners. Z is admitted as a new partner and pays Rs. 30,000 as premium for goodwill directly (privately) to X and Y. Which of the following is the treatment in the books of the firm?

options.text: No entry is passed in the books of the firm
Bank A/c Dr. To Premium for Goodwill A/c, for Rs. 30,000
Bank A/c Dr. To Z's Capital A/c, for Rs. 30,000
Goodwill A/c Dr. To X's and Y's Capital A/cs, for Rs. 30,000

candidate.explanation: If the premium is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm. The entries debiting Bank A/c apply when the amount is paid through the firm, and the Goodwill A/c entry distributing goodwill to the sacrificing partners belongs to the through-the-firm treatment as well. Here the amount is paid directly, so options B, C and D are not required.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Partnership Accounts - Admission of a Partner
learning_objective.objective: Identify the accounting treatment of premium for goodwill paid privately by a new partner.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company issues debentures that are payable in a lump sum on the expiry of 10 years and that carry a charge on a specific machine held for use in operations. How are these debentures correctly described?

options.text: Secured with a floating charge; redeemable
Unsecured; irredeemable
Secured with a fixed charge; redeemable
Secured with a fixed charge; irredeemable

candidate.explanation: A charge on a specific asset is a fixed charge, and debentures with a charge created on company assets are secured; a floating charge is on the general assets, so A is wrong. Unsecured debentures have no specific charge on assets, so B is wrong. Debentures payable on the expiry of a specific period in lump sum are redeemable, whereas irredeemable debentures carry no undertaking for repayment, so D is wrong.

learning_objective.objective: Classify debentures by security and by tenure.

candidate.explanation: Under the Average Profits Method, goodwill is the past average profits multiplied by the number of years of anticipated profits. Because the first year's profit is already being earned, only 3 years remain to be counted, so goodwill = 45,000 x 3 = Rs. 1,35,000.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: P and Q share profits in the ratio 2 : 1. On dissolution of the firm, the balance sheet shows a General Reserve of Rs. 30,000. How is it transferred to the partners' capital accounts?

options.text: P's Capital Rs. 10,000 and Q's Capital Rs. 20,000
P's Capital Rs. 20,000 and Q's Capital Rs. 10,000
P's Capital Rs. 15,000 and Q's Capital Rs. 15,000
Credit Realisation A/c with Rs. 30,000

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: Which statement about the economic objectives of a business, as described in the NCERT text on management, is correct?

options.text: Survival requires the organisation to earn enough revenues to cover its costs.
Growth means a business should avoid adding to its prospects in the long run.
Once an organisation survives, making a profit is no longer necessary.
Survival, profit and growth are the three social objectives of a business.

candidate.explanation: The excerpt states that, in order to survive, an organisation must earn enough revenues to cover costs. It says a business needs to add to its prospects in the long run, so B is contradicted. It says mere survival is not enough and management has to ensure a profit, so C is contradicted. It names survival, profit and growth as the economic objectives of a business, so D is contradicted.

learning_objective.objective: Explain the economic objectives of management: survival, profit and growth.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body:
Consider the two statements.
Statement 1: Because an organisation interacts with social, economic and political factors in its external environment, it must change itself and its goals according to the needs of the environment.
Statement 2: The effect of management cannot be noticed in an organisation, since management is an intangible force.
Which option is correct?

options.text: Only Statement 2 is correct.
Only Statement 1 is correct.
Both Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct.

candidate.explanation: Statement 1 matches the excerpt on management as a dynamic function: the organisation interacts with social, economic and political factors and must change itself and its goals according to the needs of the environment. Statement 2 is contradicted by the excerpt on intangibility, which says the effect of management is noticeable where targets are met according to plans, employees are happy and satisfied, and there is orderliness. So only Statement 1 is correct.

learning_objective.objective: Describe the characteristics of management, including that it is a dynamic function and an intangible force.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: In a company, the accounting staff initially resisted a new accounting system introduced by a manager. The manager explained the purpose, provided training and motivated the staff with additional rewards, after which the staff accepted the change and cooperated. Which conclusion is supported by the NCERT excerpt on directing?

options.text: People generally welcome changes in the organisation, so the staff's resistance was unusual.
Directing techniques should bring out the energies of only a few selected employees.
Effective directing through motivation, communication and leadership helps reduce resistance to change and develop cooperation.
Training and additional rewards should be avoided because they increase resistance to change.

candidate.explanation: The excerpt says effective directing through motivation, communication and leadership helps to reduce resistance to change and develop the required cooperation, and uses this same example. It says people generally tend to resist changes, so A is contradicted. The principle of maximum individual contribution says directing must help every individual contribute to his maximum potential, so B is contradicted. In the example, explaining the purpose, training and additional rewards lead employees to accept the change, so D is contradicted.

learning_objective.objective: Explain the importance of directing in reducing resistance to change.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: Veda Retail, an existing enterprise, has created new jobs by opening two outlets, and some of its existing employees have left the organisation. Which statement about its staffing is supported by the NCERT excerpts?

options.text: Staffing was a one-time activity that ended when the enterprise began operating.
Staffing covers only permanent employees and excludes daily wagers, consultants and contract employees.
Succession planning for managers works against the continuous survival and growth of the enterprise.
Staffing is a continuous process because new jobs may be created and some existing employees may leave.

candidate.explanation: The excerpt states that in an existing enterprise staffing is a continuous process because new jobs may be created and some of the existing employees may leave, which matches Veda Retail. A is contradicted by this. B is contradicted because staffing may involve any combination of employees including daily wagers, consultants and contract employees. C is contradicted because succession planning for managers is listed as ensuring the continuous survival and growth of the enterprise.

learning_objective.objective: Explain why staffing is a continuous process and state its importance.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: Meera paid the full price for a mobile phone ordered through a shopping website for her personal use and gave it to her mother, who uses it with Meera's approval. Dev ordered 20 phones from the same website to resell them in his shop. All the phones were defective. Which statement is correct under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 as described in the NCERT excerpts?

options.text: Meera and her mother are within the scope of the Act, while Dev, who bought for resale, is outside it.
Meera, her mother and Dev are all consumers, because the Act applies to both offline and online transactions.
Meera is covered, but her mother is not, because she did not buy the phone herself.
None of the three is covered, because the Act applies only to offline transactions.

candidate.explanation: The excerpt says the Act applies to both offline and online transactions and includes any user of the goods if the use is made with the approval of the buyer, so Meera and her mother are covered. A person who obtains goods for resale or commercial purpose is not treated as a consumer and is outside the scope of the Act, which applies to Dev. B fails because of the resale exclusion, C because users with the buyer's approval are included, and D because online transactions are covered.

learning_objective.objective: Identify who is treated as a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act 2019.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: A central bank sells securities through an agreement that specifies the date and price at which it will repurchase them, instead of making an outright sale. The rate at which money is withdrawn in this manner is called the:

options.text: Repo rate
Reverse repo rate
Bank rate
Outright sale rate

candidate.explanation: The excerpt states that selling securities through an agreement specifying the date and price of repurchase is a reverse repurchase agreement, and the rate at which money is withdrawn this way is the reverse repo rate. The repo rate is the rate at which money is lent when the central bank buys a security with a resale agreement, which is the opposite direction. The bank rate is the rate at which the RBI gives loans to commercial banks, not a rate at which money is withdrawn. The stem says the arrangement is instead of an outright sale, so an outright sale rate does not describe it.

learning_objective.objective: Distinguish repo and reverse repo operations as instruments of the central bank.

candidate.body: A country's exports of goods are Rs 120 crore and its imports of goods are Rs 150 crore. Taking net exports (NX) as exports minus imports, the country has:

A trade surplus of Rs 270 crore
A trade deficit of Rs 30 crore
A trade deficit of Rs 270 crore

candidate.explanation: NX = exports - imports = 120 - 150 = -30, so NX is negative with imports exceeding exports. The excerpt states that a negative NX implies a trade deficit, so the deficit is Rs 30 crore. A surplus would need exports greater than imports, which the stem contradicts. Rs 270 crore comes from adding 120 and 150 instead of subtracting.

learning_objective.objective: Compute net exports and interpret a trade surplus or deficit.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: In a perfectly competitive market for wheat, market demand is qD = 200 - p and market supply is qS = 120 + p (quantities in kg, price p in rupees per kg, with p at least 10). If the price is fixed at Rs 60 per kg, the market shows:

options.text: Excess supply of 40 kg
Excess demand of 40 kg
Excess supply of 60 kg
Equilibrium, with the market clearing at Rs 60

candidate.explanation: Setting qD = qS gives 200 - p = 120 + p, so the equilibrium price is Rs 40 per kg. Rs 60 is greater than the equilibrium price, and at a price greater than p* there is excess supply, so excess demand and equilibrium at Rs 60 are ruled out. At Rs 60, qD = 140 and qS = 180, so excess supply is 180 - 140 = 40 kg, not 60 kg.

learning_objective.objective: Find equilibrium price from linear demand and supply and identify excess supply at a higher price.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
candidate.body: A firm in a perfectly competitive market faces a market price of Rs 25 per unit. Its marginal cost rises with output: the marginal cost is Rs 15 at 10 units, Rs 25 at 20 units, Rs 35 at 30 units and Rs 50 at 40 units. Which output level maximises the firm's profit?

options.text: 40 units
30 units
10 units
20 units

candidate.explanation: For a perfectly competitive firm MR = P = Rs 25, and profit is maximum where MR = MC, which is where P = MC. This happens at 20 units, where MC is Rs 25. At 10 units MC (Rs 15) is below MR, and as long as MR is greater than MC profits are increasing, so 10 units is not the maximum. At 30 and 40 units MC (Rs 35 and Rs 50) exceeds MR, and when MR is less than MC profits fall.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
learning_objective.objective: Apply the P = MC rule to find the profit-maximising output of a competitive firm.

candidate.subject: english
candidate.body: According to the passage, why did the repair club buy a charging cable and switches instead of a new drill?

options.text: The inventory check showed that the existing drill could not be repaired at all.
The existing drill lacked only a charging cable, and waiting repairs needed inexpensive switches.
The minutes stated that buying new equipment is always wasteful for a club.
The members agreed never to reconsider the purchase of a new drill.

candidate.explanation: The passage says the existing drill worked but lacked a charging cable, while several repairs were waiting for inexpensive switches. The minutes did not claim that buying new equipment was always wasteful, and members agreed to reconsider the drill purchase if the repaired equipment could no longer handle their workload. So the other options contradict the passage.
candidate.passage_text: A fictional repair club allocated its weekly budget to tools and replacement parts. Members initially proposed buying a new drill. The inventory check then showed that an existing drill worked but lacked a charging cable, while several repairs were waiting for inexpensive switches. The club bought the cable and switches instead. This allowed it to resume the waiting repairs without exhausting the budget. The minutes explained that the decision concerned the club's immediate needs; they did not claim that buying new equipment was always wasteful. Members agreed to reconsider the drill purchase if the repaired equipment could no longer handle their workload.

learning_objective.objective: Identify the reason for a decision stated in a factual passage.

options.text: They had no other departure available, because the earlier departure on every route was removed.
They were promised shorter waits than before, because the notice favoured all finishing times equally.
They gained a faster journey, because the notice presented the later departure as quicker.
They waited longer for the shifted departure but could choose the earlier departure kept on another route.

The school shifted one departure from 4:00 to 4:15, allowing pupils in a late laboratory session to reach it. Pupils whose classes ended earlier consequently waited longer. The school retained an earlier departure on another route and asked students to choose the departure suited to their class schedule. candidate.subject: english
candidate.body: Why did the archive record visitors' memories separately as possible identifications?

options.text: A memory alone lacked a dated label or document, so it could be kept without being presented as established fact.
The archive discarded any memory that was not supported by a dated label or an accompanying document.
Confirmation required the visitor to feel confident about the recollection being offered.
A letter had to confirm every identification before the archive could record it.

candidate.explanation: The passage says a description was stored as confirmed only when a dated label or an accompanying document identified its subject, and that visitors' memories were recorded separately as possible identifications. The archivist explained that preserving a recollection did not require presenting it as established fact.
